newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian truckers say strike plans firm.
newsitem.headline: Colombian truckers say strike plans firm.

text.p: The head of Colombia's main truck drivers' union said Friday there was no change in plans to stage a nationwide strike beginning at midnight Saturday.

Javier Suarez, head of Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), spoke after he and other union bosses held about two hours of closed-door talks with Interior Minister Horacio Serpa at the minister's office in the historic city center.
"Except for the goodwill shown by the minister, in trying to bring the two sides together, there have been no changes," Suarez told Reuters.
"Plans for the immobilization remain firm," he added, saying the ACC, which represents about 80 percent of the country's truck drivers, still intended to go ahead with the work stoppage.

Suarez said another round of talks had been scheduled for later in the day, at the Transportation Ministry, but the government had failed so far to come up with any new proposals that might avert a strike.
The ACC called the strike in March on grounds that the government, and private transportation companies, had violated terms of an agreement that ended a crippling 11-day stoppage last October.
The previous strike paralyzed virtually all of the country's highway freight, and including about 200,000 60-kilo bags of coffee.

Transportation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez said Thursday that the government may declare a new strike illegal. The October strike was outlawed as well, however, and it had no effect in terms of getting drivers back to work. ((-- Juan Guillermo Londono, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
